newsitem.title: UK: Smith&Nephew extends fall as bid talk quashed.
newsitem.headline: Smith&Nephew extends fall as bid talk quashed.

text.p: Shares in healthcare company Smith & Nephew Plc extended their early losses on Tuesday after the company said takeover rumours surrounding it lacked any foundation.
"There is no basis at all for these rumours," chief executive John Robinson told Reuters.
The shares were 7-1/2p weaker at 183-1/2 by 1245 GMT.
"The shares have been pushed up by speculative buying over the last few months by people looking for a bid," one market-maker said. "Some of those people are getting out now."
Earlier, the shares dipped after Smith & Nephew announced a one-percent rise in annual pre-tax profits to 182.2 million pounds, at the low end of expectations.
Alyson Coates, analyst at SocGen, said the strong pound and launch costs of S&N's new Dermagraft bio-engineered skin tissue replacement product would restrict profit growth in the current year.

"The company is developing its exposure in developing markets but it is still working hard to deliver underlying growth in the mid-single-digit range," Coates said, adding that benefits from Dermagraft would probably not fully emerge until 1998.
However she said the company was well-placed to make an acquisition, with gearing of just 15 percent.

Peter Cartwright, analyst at Williams de Broe, said there was no immediate reason from the results to change his "hold" stance on the stock. He said the statement was in line with S&N's trading statement in January.
"The picture looks as if it will improve in 1998," Cartwright said, "but that is sufficiently far enough away for there to be no hurry to get involved."
Smith & Nephew said its underlying sales rose six percent in a year when market conditions were "if anything, tougher than 1995".
It said conditions in its main markets were likely to remain tough for some time, although "these markets remain intrinsically sound with above-average, long-term growth prospects."
